# mibz2

> A bzip2 decoder built for memory-level parallelism.

mibz2 is a bzip2 decoder, block-parallel, its inverse BWT walked as interleaved chains
within each block, with byte-for-byte libbzip2 output and every block and stream CRC
checked, from Python (`mibz2.decompress`, `mibz2.open`) or Rust (`mibz2::decode`,
`mibz2::BzReader`). Install with `pip install mibz2` or `cargo add mibz2`. Each link below
is the Markdown version of a page of https://lmmx.github.io/mibz2/.

## Benchmarks

- [Benchmarks](<https://lmmx.github.io/mibz2/pr-preview/pr-1282/benchmarks/index.md>): How mibz2's CI benchmark measures the decoder: the corpora, the rounds, the paired ratios and the modelled full-dump figure.
- [History](<https://lmmx.github.io/mibz2/pr-preview/pr-1282/benchmarks/history/index.md>): mibz2's decoding speed, CPU time and peak memory, merge by merge: each merged pull request's own paired benchmark, chained, and master's absolute figures on one runner at a time.
- [Alternatives](<https://lmmx.github.io/mibz2/pr-preview/pr-1282/benchmarks/alternatives/index.md>): mibz2 beside other bzip2 decoders on master's latest benchmark run: paired ratios with 95% intervals, per corpus and thread count.
- [Throughput–memory frontier](<https://lmmx.github.io/mibz2/pr-preview/pr-1282/benchmarks/frontier/index.md>): Whether mibz2 can decode faster with less memory when blocks share the cache: the question, the method, and what has been measured so far.

## Concepts

- [Concepts](<https://lmmx.github.io/mibz2/pr-preview/pr-1282/concepts/index.md>): What mibz2 decodes, what it checks, and how it decodes in parallel.
- [Why 32 couriers beat one](<https://lmmx.github.io/mibz2/pr-preview/pr-1282/concepts/couriers/index.md>): mibz2's premise, memory-level parallelism in the inverse BWT, explained through couriers and a dispatcher: independent lanes, prefetching, the per-step cost that binds next, and the measurements.
- [What is checked, and when](<https://lmmx.github.io/mibz2/pr-preview/pr-1282/concepts/checks/index.md>): Which CRCs mibz2 checks and when, what its errors report, and the inputs it refuses.
- [How it works](<https://lmmx.github.io/mibz2/pr-preview/pr-1282/concepts/how-it-works/index.md>): mibz2's scanner thread, its workers, and the inverse BWT walked as interleaved chains.
- [Prior work](<https://lmmx.github.io/mibz2/pr-preview/pr-1282/concepts/prior-work/index.md>): The work mibz2 builds on: libbzip2's format and checks, Kärkkäinen, Kempa and Puglisi's interleaved BWT inversion, and lbzip2's and pbzip2's block parallelism.

## Get started

- [Installation](<https://lmmx.github.io/mibz2/pr-preview/pr-1282/getting-started/installation/index.md>): Install mibz2 from PyPI or crates.io.
- [Quickstart](<https://lmmx.github.io/mibz2/pr-preview/pr-1282/getting-started/quickstart/index.md>): Decode a .bz2 file with mibz2 from Python and from Rust.

## Optional

- [Blog](<https://lmmx.github.io/mibz2/pr-preview/pr-1282/blog/index.md>): What mibz2's experiments are finding, and where they go next.
- [26× faster Python line reads in abi3](<https://lmmx.github.io/mibz2/pr-preview/pr-1282/blog/2026-11-28-python-line-delivery-stable-abi/index.md>): Bypassing Python's redundant buffering layer and scanning newlines in safe Rust speeds up line reads up to twenty-six times while keeping one universal abi3 wheel.
- [Shrinking worker scratch speeds the scanner](<https://lmmx.github.io/mibz2/pr-preview/pr-1282/blog/2026-11-28-shrinking-worker-scratch-speeds-the-scanner/index.md>): Shrinking each worker's slab scratch removes almost every extra cache stall on the serial scanner, making the whole eight-worker decode faster.
- [Clock hysteresis and memory noise](<https://lmmx.github.io/mibz2/pr-preview/pr-1282/blog/2026-11-28-clock-modes-and-memory-noise/index.md>): A brief pause between runs can trap a desktop processor below full boost, while parallel queue jitter dominates peak memory across six server chips.
- [Walking the BWT cycle forward across four lanes](<https://lmmx.github.io/mibz2/pr-preview/pr-1282/blog/2026-11-28-four-lanes-forward/index.md>): Walking the inverse BWT cycle forward across four safe Rust lanes lets workers outrun the serial scanner, alongside three default speedups.
- [Why compression ratio moves the scaling ceiling](<https://lmmx.github.io/mibz2/pr-preview/pr-1282/blog/2026-11-27-why-the-scaling-ceiling-moves/index.md>): On a ten-core processor, the same parallel bzip2 decoder scales to nine threads on structured dumps yet peaks at five on ordinary source code and text.
- [Half the memory on compressible files](<https://lmmx.github.io/mibz2/pr-preview/pr-1282/blog/2026-11-27-bounded-memory-on-highly-compressible-input/index.md>): Workers that pause rather than race far ahead of the reader now let mibz2 unpack a tiny file of runs in half the memory, and sooner as well.
- [Faster decoding for ordinary text](<https://lmmx.github.io/mibz2/pr-preview/pr-1282/blog/2026-11-27-faster-decoding-for-ordinary-text/index.md>): Our fastest kernel passes over five in six blocks of ordinary text, so mibz2 now foresees its refusals and gives the general-purpose path a speed-up of its own.
- [Stages built to fit together](<https://lmmx.github.io/mibz2/pr-preview/pr-1282/blog/2026-11-27-stages-built-to-fit-together/index.md>): Rebuilt so that each stage hands the next exactly what it needs, the prototype stages of mibz2's workers save time that adds up almost exactly.
- [The decoder's true floor and a pooled scan](<https://lmmx.github.io/mibz2/pr-preview/pr-1282/blog/2026-11-26-true-floor-and-pooled-scan/index.md>): Zero-copy stand-ins drop mibz2's plumbing floor to 5 milliseconds and uncover hidden spelling and cache costs, while pooling the scan pays off only from slack.
- [Dropping the coordinator](<https://lmmx.github.io/mibz2/pr-preview/pr-1282/blog/2026-11-26-dropping-the-coordinator/index.md>): Our coordinating agent wrote 46% of recent team traffic, so we replaced central routing with atomic file locks and fresh sessions on a shared frontier.
- [The experiment](<https://lmmx.github.io/mibz2/pr-preview/pr-1282/blog/2026-11-26-complementary-bottlenecks/index.md>): Making the parts of mibz2's decoder free in turn and in combination shows where new algorithms would pay off and which two stages are worth far more together.
- [Beyond it: the algorithms](<https://lmmx.github.io/mibz2/pr-preview/pr-1282/blog/2026-11-26-from-bottlenecks-to-better-algorithms/index.md>): How the matrix's lessons could become new algorithms, from what the experiment left behind to four designs and the tests that would reject them.
- [The story](<https://lmmx.github.io/mibz2/pr-preview/pr-1282/blog/2026-11-25-the-decoder-as-a-queueing-network/index.md>): Modelled as stations and queues, the decoder shows in advance where more workers stop helping and which experiments to run next.
- [Beneath it: the theory](<https://lmmx.github.io/mibz2/pr-preview/pr-1282/blog/2026-11-25-the-decoder-as-a-queueing-network-notes/index.md>): The theory under the story, from counting what waits and finding the bottleneck to pricing a change before it is built.
- [Posing the inversion problem](<https://lmmx.github.io/mibz2/pr-preview/pr-1282/blog/2026-11-24-posing-the-inversion-problem/index.md>): The search for a new inversion algorithm became an eight-step programme, from a cost referee and measured ceilings to the model that will say where new mathematics fits.
- [Masked bottlenecks](<https://lmmx.github.io/mibz2/pr-preview/pr-1282/blog/2026-11-24-the-scanner-hides-the-emitter/index.md>): Supplying both the serial scanner's output and the emission codes cuts whole-decoder time by 26% at ten workers, more than either stage supplied alone.
- [What else moves together](<https://lmmx.github.io/mibz2/pr-preview/pr-1282/blog/2026-11-24-what-else-moves-together/index.md>): The next decoder for bzip2's block sort will come from rows that move together in a new sense, or from inversion steps that yield more information.
- [Halving the single-row steps](<https://lmmx.github.io/mibz2/pr-preview/pr-1282/blog/2026-11-24-halving-the-single-row-steps/index.md>): We now search for a new way to undo bzip2's block sort by forbidding the obvious mechanism and asking whether any exact decoder can do without it.
- [Playing the hand you're dealt](<https://lmmx.github.io/mibz2/pr-preview/pr-1282/blog/2026-11-22-decompression-is-the-harder-problem/index.md>): A discussion of the mibz2 swarm, and why the Hutter Prize has it backwards: it rewards whoever stacks the deck best, when real data deals you the hand.
- [Correctness is uniform, cost is not](<https://lmmx.github.io/mibz2/pr-preview/pr-1282/blog/2026-11-22-correctness-is-uniform-cost-is-not/index.md>): Every route in mibz2's bzip2 decoder is exact on every block, but cost varies from block to block and so we hunt for speed in many places.
- [Two centuries of tools](<https://lmmx.github.io/mibz2/pr-preview/pr-1282/blog/2026-11-22-two-centuries-of-tools/index.md>): A claimed Riemann proof built one new idea on fifty older tools reaching back two centuries, so our research teams now look back as hard as forward.
- [Admitting dense blocks to Open](<https://lmmx.github.io/mibz2/pr-preview/pr-1282/blog/2026-11-21-a-memory-gain-is-a-gain/index.md>): A bounded admission band takes five dense blocks off a 5.6 MiB-per-worker fallback, and the decoder runs slightly faster in over a quarter less memory.
- [Besieging hard problems](<https://lmmx.github.io/mibz2/pr-preview/pr-1282/blog/2026-11-21-besieging-hard-problems/index.md>): A machine-checked Riemann proof shows how far a search can range once checking is cheap, so ours now begins by making speed cheap to check.
- [Fast alone, slow in a crowd](<https://lmmx.github.io/mibz2/pr-preview/pr-1282/blog/2026-11-21-fast-alone-slow-in-a-crowd/index.md>): Walking each block in eight lanes made our newest decoding loop 13% faster on one thread, yet 5% slower once eight workers shared the processor.
- [Sixteen at a stroke](<https://lmmx.github.io/mibz2/pr-preview/pr-1282/blog/2026-11-21-sixteen-at-a-stroke/index.md>): Writing sixteen at a stroke and keeping only what it needs spares the processor a guess per run, so mibz2 0.5.8 decodes Wikidata 5% faster on ten cores.
- [Research by obligation](<https://lmmx.github.io/mibz2/pr-preview/pr-1282/blog/2026-11-20-research-by-obligation/index.md>): We now track the work any decoder must pay for rather than the algorithms that pay it, and a claimed Riemann proof has sharpened how we hunt.
- [Where the decoding work goes](<https://lmmx.github.io/mibz2/pr-preview/pr-1282/blog/2026-11-20-where-the-decoding-work-goes/index.md>): Tracing each costly row back to the text it spells shows that JSON keys cost almost nothing, while random statement IDs claim two thirds of the hardest rows.
- [Train tracks](<https://lmmx.github.io/mibz2/pr-preview/pr-1282/blog/2026-11-20-train-tracks/index.md>): Thurston's train tracks squeeze a tangle of curves onto a few weighted branches that can be edited directly, and a compressed block's runs form something very like one.
- [Open Returns](<https://lmmx.github.io/mibz2/pr-preview/pr-1282/blog/2026-11-19-open-returns/index.md>): mibz2 0.5.7 decodes Wikidata up to 11% faster on ten cores by keeping a tenth of each block's rows and letting the rest travel together in convoys.
- [What decoding pays for](<https://lmmx.github.io/mibz2/pr-preview/pr-1282/blog/2026-11-18-what-decoding-pays-for/index.md>): Three ways of undoing bzip2's block sort spend about two operations per run, and how long run boundaries persist explains much of why Cells and the forest vary.
- [Cutting the loop open](<https://lmmx.github.io/mibz2/pr-preview/pr-1282/blog/2026-11-18-cutting-the-loop-open/index.md>): Snip the decoder's one long loop open and most of each Wikidata block falls into bundled paths, where one traced letter spells about sixteen.
- [Technical notes](<https://lmmx.github.io/mibz2/pr-preview/pr-1282/blog/2026-11-18-cutting-the-loop-open-notes/index.md>): Technical notes to the post on cutting the loop open: the bundle bound and its tight cases, one strip's heights, the two constructors of the open paths, the narrow–wide switch cut, and what the two verifications checked.
- [Raising the knee](<https://lmmx.github.io/mibz2/pr-preview/pr-1282/blog/2026-11-17-raising-the-knee/index.md>): mibz2 0.5.4 now speeds up until all ten physical cores of its test processor are busy, then holds level on the whole machine up to twenty threads.
- [Modelling the cache](<https://lmmx.github.io/mibz2/pr-preview/pr-1282/blog/2026-11-17-modelling-the-cache-to-rightsize-workers/index.md>): mibz2 now runs fewer workers than threads on a ten-core desktop and finishes sooner, while a cache model is tested to pick the count on any machine.
- [Technical notes](<https://lmmx.github.io/mibz2/pr-preview/pr-1282/blog/2026-11-17-modelling-the-cache-to-rightsize-workers-notes/index.md>): Technical notes to the post on modelling the cache to rightsize workers: the contention–parallelism trade-off and its sensitivity, what the contention-associated overhead is made of, the full ledger of frozen predictions, the CPU bound's history, and topology and transfer.
- [A mathematical dictionary](<https://lmmx.github.io/mibz2/pr-preview/pr-1282/blog/2026-11-16-mathematical-dictionary/index.md>): Our BWT inversion is not the sheaf an earlier analogy suggested, yet the places of its words form one naturally.
- [Stop and walk](<https://lmmx.github.io/mibz2/pr-preview/pr-1282/blog/2026-11-16-stop-and-walk/index.md>): Halting each block's rebuild early spares mibz2 a third of the text pieces it stores, but on ten cores the slower walk outweighs the memory saved.
- [Lazy letters](<https://lmmx.github.io/mibz2/pr-preview/pr-1282/blog/2026-11-16-lazy-letters/index.md>): Holding fewer letters at once leaves the cache less crowded, so eight to ten threads decode up to 11% faster despite extra instructions.
- [The free closure of an induction](<https://lmmx.github.io/mibz2/pr-preview/pr-1282/blog/2026-11-15-free-closure/index.md>): The steps that cost mibz2 no bookkeeping can be taken in any order and still meet at one end point, now proved to belong to the block itself.
- [The width of an induction](<https://lmmx.github.io/mibz2/pr-preview/pr-1282/blog/2026-11-15-induction-width/index.md>): Taking the steps that cost no bookkeeping first would let mibz2 rebuild a block while keeping about a third as much in memory at its busiest moment.
- [Removing duplicated interval lengths and text references](<https://lmmx.github.io/mibz2/pr-preview/pr-1282/blog/2026-11-15-bottom-slots/index.md>): mibz2 tracks each run of equal bytes in two orders, and a run's entry in the second shrinks from 20 bytes to 8 by pointing to the first.
- [Reduce, reuse, recycle](<https://lmmx.github.io/mibz2/pr-preview/pr-1282/blog/2026-11-15-slot-recycling/index.md>): Each new text fragment takes over the slot its finished neighbour just vacated, so mibz2 touches 30% fewer slots and needs up to 15% less memory.
- [Companion: compact programs](<https://lmmx.github.io/mibz2/pr-preview/pr-1282/blog/2026-11-12-rauzy-technical-companion/index.md>): This technical companion traces how compact word programs reconstruct text from the BWT, including the costs and limits of building and expanding them.
- [The post](<https://lmmx.github.io/mibz2/pr-preview/pr-1282/blog/2026-11-10-rauzy-veech-reconstruction/index.md>): An experimental mibz2 kernel rebuilds bzip2 text without a row-by-row walk, from reusable word rules that form the block's Lyndon tree.
- [mibz2 gets a pit crew](<https://lmmx.github.io/mibz2/pr-preview/pr-1282/blog/2026-11-09-pit-crew-service-threads/index.md>): Handing each block's serial steps to two dedicated threads gives mibz2 a rare double win, decoding 4.5% faster on ten cores with 13% less CPU.
- [Reading the BWT's runs off the MTF codes](<https://lmmx.github.io/mibz2/pr-preview/pr-1282/blog/2026-11-08-bwt-runs-from-mtf-codes/index.md>): bzip2's move-to-front codes mark where each run of the BWT's last column starts, so the runs could be listed without writing the column. It is not built.
- [One shift per run](<https://lmmx.github.io/mibz2/pr-preview/pr-1282/blog/2026-11-08-inverse-bwt-navigation/index.md>): The inverse BWT's next-row map is one shift per run of equal bytes, so it can be stored per run rather than per row. Whether that beats mibz2's table is unproven.
- [Technical appendix](<https://lmmx.github.io/mibz2/pr-preview/pr-1282/blog/2026-11-08-inverse-bwt-navigation-notes/index.md>): Technical appendix to the post on inverse-BWT navigation: the select reduction, consecutive entries and sparse corrections, entropy and run-count space bounds, compact30's records, several steps at once, cycles and necklaces, the permutree thesis, and correctness oracles.
- [Pipelined teams in mibz2 0.2.6](<https://lmmx.github.io/mibz2/pr-preview/pr-1282/blog/2026-11-07-pipelined-teams/index.md>): While a team's helpers invert one block, its leader finishes the last and prepares the next: 7% faster than 0.2.5 on ten cores, for 5% more processor time.
- [Why mibz2 stops scaling at eight threads](<https://lmmx.github.io/mibz2/pr-preview/pr-1282/blog/2026-11-07-why-mibz2-stops-scaling/index.md>): Each block decoded at once slows the others, and more threads per block barely help, so three teams of three beat four of two by 9%. Why blocks interfere is open.
- [Huffman decoding: the bit buffer in a register](<https://lmmx.github.io/mibz2/pr-preview/pr-1282/blog/2026-11-05-huffman-bit-buffer/index.md>): The Huffman decoder wrote its bit buffer to memory and read it back at every lookup. Kept in a register, the stage ran 13% faster on Intel and 5% on AMD.
- [An autonomous agent team](<https://lmmx.github.io/mibz2/pr-preview/pr-1282/blog/2026-11-04-autonomous-agent-team/index.md>): Each of four agents does one part of the research. A GitHub doorbell lets them hand work to each other directly, without me acting as their message bus.
- [From 49 instructions to 12](<https://lmmx.github.io/mibz2/pr-preview/pr-1282/blog/2026-11-04-compact30-constructor/index.md>): Writing a cheap placeholder for each row, and finishing each 30-row group once, shrank the inner loop. It still builds too slowly.
- [Technical appendix](<https://lmmx.github.io/mibz2/pr-preview/pr-1282/blog/2026-11-04-compact30-constructor-notes/index.md>): Technical appendix to the post on building a smaller bzip2 decoding table: the BWT's navigation table from first principles, stable counting sort, compact30's row labels, records and RAW groups, epochs and snapshots, finishing a group, RAW canonicalisation, and why fewer instructions needn't mean less time.
- [BWT space–time tradeoff](<https://lmmx.github.io/mibz2/pr-preview/pr-1282/blog/2026-11-02-revisiting-space-time-tradeoff-bwt-inversion/index.md>): A packed table saved memory but cost too much to read. A cheaper compact lookup gives the first positive traversal result.
- [Instructions, overlap and evidence](<https://lmmx.github.io/mibz2/pr-preview/pr-1282/blog/2026-11-02-memory-level-parallelism/index.md>): Interleaving pointer chases lets memory waits overlap. The speedup shows that this pays, but not what limits it: a 2022 exchange about Daniel Lemire's benchmark, read against mibz2's inverse-BWT walk.
- [Technical appendix](<https://lmmx.github.io/mibz2/pr-preview/pr-1282/blog/2026-11-02-memory-level-parallelism-notes/index.md>): Technical appendix to the memory-level parallelism post: the disagreement about ILP and MLP in detail, the 2022 benchmark, throughput models, Intel counter definitions, a measurement programme for mibz2, a reading list and the source register.
- [Inverse-BWT memory interference](<https://lmmx.github.io/mibz2/pr-preview/pr-1282/blog/2026-11-01-inverse-bwt-memory-interference/index.md>): Four workers finish decompression sooner, but together spend 32% more processor time per byte. We're testing whether competition for shared memory is responsible.
- [Block dispatch in mibz2](<https://lmmx.github.io/mibz2/pr-preview/pr-1282/blog/2026-11-01-block-dispatch/index.md>): How mibz2's parallel decoder hands blocks to its workers, why some take up to a millisecond to be picked up, and how to tell lock contention from scheduling delay.
- [32 lanes, 8.6 chains](<https://lmmx.github.io/mibz2/pr-preview/pr-1282/blog/2026-10-31-room-walk-overlap/index.md>): The decoder's 32-lane walk runs 8.6 times faster than one chain. That figure may not mean what it seems: the walk may already hide memory latency, and spend too many instructions on each byte.
- [Compact navigation tables for the inverse BWT](<https://lmmx.github.io/mibz2/pr-preview/pr-1282/blog/2026-10-29-compact-navigation-tables/index.md>): Most of the inverse BWT's navigation table follows simple patterns: what a census of real blocks found, and what comes next.
- [History](<https://lmmx.github.io/mibz2/pr-preview/pr-1282/background/history/index.md>): Where mibz2 came from: written in wikidata-pq to decode the Wikidata dump, then moved to a repository of its own.
- [Status](<https://lmmx.github.io/mibz2/pr-preview/pr-1282/background/status/index.md>): Where mibz2's research stands: the cooperative inverse BWT found, confirmed and explained on a 10-core workstation, and what comes next.
- [Behind the scenes](<https://lmmx.github.io/mibz2/pr-preview/pr-1282/background/behind-the-scenes/index.md>): What mibz2's agent team is doing, and why, as the team's observer last wrote it down, with the record it rests on and every earlier version.
- [Journals](<https://lmmx.github.io/mibz2/pr-preview/pr-1282/background/journals/index.md>): mibz2's development journals: where they are and what each one records.
- [Development](<https://lmmx.github.io/mibz2/pr-preview/pr-1282/maintainers/development/index.md>): The repository's layout, how to build, test and benchmark mibz2, and the commit conventions.
- [Documentation](<https://lmmx.github.io/mibz2/pr-preview/pr-1282/maintainers/documentation/index.md>): How the documentation site and its benchmark pages are built, checked, tested and published to GitHub Pages.
- [Releasing](<https://lmmx.github.io/mibz2/pr-preview/pr-1282/maintainers/releasing/index.md>): How mibz2 is released to crates.io and PyPI at one version: Deploy Release, Tag Release and Release Notes.

## Reference

- [Reference](<https://lmmx.github.io/mibz2/pr-preview/pr-1282/reference/index.md>): mibz2's API in Python and in Rust.
- [mibz2 (Python)](<https://lmmx.github.io/mibz2/pr-preview/pr-1282/reference/api/mibz2/index.md>): The mibz2 Python package: decompress, open, BZ2Reader and DecodeError.
- [mibz2 (Rust)](<https://lmmx.github.io/mibz2/pr-preview/pr-1282/reference/rust/index.md>): The mibz2 Rust crate: decode, decode_parallel, BzReader, StreamDecoder, scan, decode_blocks and Error.
